items.claim: The decision to keep the wisdom coda attached rests in part on a barred use of the single-witness paragraph layer, and the row never weighs the fourfold divine-title chain that stops exactly at the seam it calls its own central judgment call.
items.evidence: The first reason offered is byte-true and I confirm it: no woe-cry, oracle-header or messenger formula stands at web:Isa.50.10 (sweep: woe-cry 22 verses book-wide, 0 in chs 49-52; oracle-header skeleton 15 verses book-wide, 0 in chs 49-52; messenger formula 48 verses book-wide, 8 in chs 49-52, of which ch 50's only site is oshb:Isa.50.1). The second reason is not admissible in the form given: the row holds the coda attached partly 'because the parashah paragraph ... carries no internal break at web:Isa.50.10' -- an affirmative boundary reason built on the ABSENCE of a mark in a layer that is weak corroboration only in the Prophets and whose absence is never counterevidence. The marks themselves are cited correctly against the inventory (SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.50.3, PE at oshb:Isa.50.11, none between), and no ketiv/qere note stands anywhere in ch 50, so nothing further is owed there. What is unengaged is the decisive byte evidence on the rival the row discloses: the divine title אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה / אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ stands at exactly four verses in ch 50 -- oshb:Isa.50.4, oshb:Isa.50.5, oshb:Isa.50.7, oshb:Isa.50.9 (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier; the byte-tier pair is oshb:Isa.50.5 with oshb:Isa.50.9, oshb:Isa.50.4 carrying the plene spelling יְהֹוִ֗ה) -- and is absent from web:Isa.50.10-Isa.50.11. The chain terminates precisely at the 50:9|50:10 turn the row is adjudicating; the row splices three of its four occurrences into its own prose without ever naming the recurrence or letting it bear on the alternative it says it rejected. The servant referent is correctly left undecided, which I do not contest.

items.claim: Onset bytes and mark handling are sound, but the named three-part summons series is a blended, untiered object and the row's own closing verse carries half of a byte-tier pair reaching to web:Isa.51.11 that no row in the chain discloses.
items.evidence: Confirmed sound: the onset שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.51.1 and matches the source bytes at byte tier, and that two-token opener is byte-unique book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, byte tier). Mark handling is the best in this cluster -- the interior SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.2 is disclosed as interior even though it cuts against the span, and PE at oshb:Isa.50.11 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.3 are both typed and single-witness-labelled, so all three marks touching the span are declared; no ketiv/qere note stands in ch 51. Blended object: the series named here joins two different verbs under one label -- שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י at oshb:Isa.51.1 and שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ at oshb:Isa.51.7 against הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ at oshb:Isa.51.4 (all byte tier) -- with no tier given and no digit-bearing sweep naming what is being counted; the summons opener itself stands at four verses book-wide from accent-stripped tier down (sweep: 4 verses -- oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.46.12, oshb:Isa.51.1, oshb:Isa.51.7), two of them outside the claimed series. The parenthetical that the first and third members repeat one shape is untiered and false at byte tier: שִׁמְע֥וּ and שִׁמְע֤וּ differ in the bytes and agree only from accent-stripped tier down. Undisclosed cross-seam device: this span closes on שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ at oshb:Isa.51.3, which recurs byte-identically at oshb:Isa.51.11 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at byte tier -- oshb:Isa.35.10, oshb:Isa.51.3, oshb:Isa.51.11). Two of those three sites are the closing verses of this span and of the web:Isa.51.9-Isa.51.11 span, bracketing 51:3-51:11 across three intervening cuts; a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against it unless disclosed, and it is not disclosed here.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah, single-witness (oshb:Isa.50.11 PE; oshb:Isa.51.2, oshb:Isa.51.3 SAMEKH)

items.claim: The onset argument is byte-clean and the refusal to harmonize the two summons verbs is correct, but the row's own close seam is crossed by the tightest byte-tier device in this cluster, undisclosed, and its closing verse is byte-paired back into the cluster's first span.
items.evidence: Confirmed sound: הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.51.4, matches the source bytes at byte tier, and is unique book-wide at every tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tiers); naming it as a different verb from the preceding span's opener rather than harmonizing the two is the correct handling. Mark disclosure is symmetric and typed -- SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.3 and oshb:Isa.51.6, single-witness-labelled, with no mark interior to the span and no ketiv/qere note in ch 51. Undisclosed at the close seam: this span's closing verse and the next span's closing verse share לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה at byte tier, at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier -- oshb:Isa.51.6 and oshb:Isa.51.8), and the run sits inside a mirrored pair -- salvation-then-righteousness at oshb:Isa.51.6, righteousness-then-salvation at oshb:Isa.51.8. That is a byte-true device straddling the 51:6|51:7 cut and it argues web:Isa.51.4-Isa.51.8 as one movement, which is the rival the neighbouring rows raise in a weaker form; neither row in the pair names it. Also undisclosed: the garment simile כַּבֶּ֣גֶד stands at exactly two verses book-wide at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses -- oshb:Isa.50.9 and oshb:Isa.51.6), so this span's closing verse is byte-paired into this cluster's opening span; at skeleton tier the simile reaches three sites here (sweep: 4 verses book-wide, three of them oshb:Isa.50.9, oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8).
tier_citations: byte (le-olam pair sweep, 2 verses book-wide; garment-simile pair sweep, 2 verses book-wide)

items.claim: Two load-bearing byte claims in the boundary rationale are false: the preceding span's closing verse carries no moth-and-worm imagery, and the two summons openers do not match at byte tier.
items.evidence: First byte-false claim: the row grounds its close on 'the same moth-and-worm contrast ... that closed the series' second member', but that preceding closing verse carries כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן, 'like smoke', at oshb:Isa.51.6 (byte tier) -- not the moth עָ֔שׁ -- and carries no סָ֑ס at any tier. The moth-and-worm pair stands only in this row's own closing verse, oshb:Isa.51.8 (byte tier). This is the contained-consonant class the hazard catalogue names: the moth skeleton is a proper substring of the smoke skeleton, so a skeleton-shaped reading blends them. What the two verses actually share at byte tier is לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה -- exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier -- oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8) -- inside a mirrored righteousness/salvation pair; the row names the wrong device and gives no tier for the one it names. The nearest partner of this closing verse's moth-and-garment cluster is not in the preceding span at all but in this cluster's first span, at oshb:Isa.50.9, כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֔וּ עָ֖שׁ יֹאכְלֵֽם (skeleton tier -- the two verses share no run of two or more tokens at byte tier), an undisclosed cross-row link. Second byte-false claim: the assertion that this opener matches the series' first member's shape is untiered and false in the bytes -- שִׁמְע֤וּ at oshb:Isa.51.7 and שִׁמְע֥וּ at oshb:Isa.51.1 differ at byte tier and agree only from accent-stripped tier down. The byte-tier partner of this row's two-token opener שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ lies outside the claimed series entirely (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier -- oshb:Isa.46.3 and oshb:Isa.51.7). A recurrence claim owes its tier at write time, and this one is stated as identity. Confirmed sound: the onset is verse-initial and matches the source bytes at byte tier; SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.6 and oshb:Isa.51.8 are typed and single-witness-labelled.
tier_citations: byte (le-olam pair sweep, 2 verses; summons-opener sweep, 2 verses book-wide)

items.claim: The onset is miscounted as doubled where the cited verse carries three tokens of the imperative, the named awake series blends two stems while the same-stem partner sits outside it, and the close is contested by a byte-tier refrain twin the row does not disclose.
items.evidence: Miscount on the row's own cited bytes: the onset is called 'the doubled Qal form' עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י, but the verse the row quotes in full carries THREE tokens of that imperative -- עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י and, later in the same verse, ע֚וּרִי (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte tier; 3 tokens in the verse). The digit-bearing characterization is contradicted by the very verse cited for it, and the contrast the row draws depends on it: the later awake-cry genuinely is doubled, two tokens, הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י at oshb:Isa.51.17 (byte tier). Blended series object: the same-stem partner of this onset is not the later cry but oshb:Isa.52.1 -- the four-token run עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי עֹז֙ recurs there at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, oshb:Isa.51.9 and oshb:Isa.52.1; 1 verse at byte tier) -- whereas the later cry uses a different stem outright, הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י at oshb:Isa.51.17 (byte tier). Naming a two-member awake series across two stems while the same-stem partner falls outside it is a blended sweep object, stated with no tier and no digit. The close is under-argued: the row rejects treating web:Isa.51.11 as its own unit because that verse 'carries no imperative, vocative, or messenger formula of its own', which I confirm is byte-true as to formulas. But the verse is itself a portable refrain unit -- שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ stands byte-identically at exactly three verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, byte tier -- oshb:Isa.35.10, oshb:Isa.51.3, oshb:Isa.51.11), one of them the closing verse of this cluster's web:Isa.51.1-Isa.51.3 span -- and the whole verse is a near-twin of oshb:Isa.35.10 that is not even skeleton-equal to it (יְשׁוּב֗וּן against יְשֻׁב֗וּן; יַשִּׂיג֔וּן נָ֖סוּ against יַשִּׂ֔יגוּ וְנָ֖סוּ, byte tier at each site). The byte evidence for the rejected alternative is stronger than the row allows, and the 51:3|51:11 pair is disclosed nowhere in the chain. Confirmed sound: the onset is verse-initial; SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.8 and oshb:Isa.51.11 are typed and single-witness-labelled; the unit-type deviation is disclosed.
tier_citations: skeleton (awake-cry four-token run sweep, 2 verses book-wide)

items.claim: Every Hebrew claim reaches byte tier at its cited verse, both seams are clean in the bytes at every tier tested, and the mark disclosure is complete, typed and symmetric.
items.evidence: All three pointed splices match the source bytes at byte tier against the verses cited for them (oshb:Isa.51.12, oshb:Isa.51.15, oshb:Isa.51.16). The onset characterization is byte-exact where the neighbouring rows' are not: אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י is genuinely doubled -- two tokens, verse-initial at oshb:Isa.51.12 (byte tier). Both seams are clean: the preceding span's closing verse and this span's opening verse share no run of two or more tokens at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier and no skeleton token of three letters or more, and the same holds across oshb:Isa.51.16 | oshb:Isa.51.17. No woe-cry, oracle-header or messenger formula stands anywhere inside the span (messenger-formula sweep: 48 verses book-wide, with no site between oshb:Isa.50.1 and oshb:Isa.51.22), so the speaker-shift argument carries the seam without competition. Disclosure is complete: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.11 and oshb:Isa.51.16, both typed and single-witness-labelled; the inventory records no mark interior to 51:12-51:16 and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in chs 50-51 (sweep: 49 ketiv/qere verses book-wide, 0 in chs 50-51), so nothing further is owed in the span. Internal byte cohesion corroborates the span rather than cutting it: the heavens-and-earth founding pair recurs inside it, נוֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַיִם֮ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָרֶץ֒ at oshb:Isa.51.13 and לִנְטֹ֤עַ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלִיסֹ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ at oshb:Isa.51.16 (byte tier at each). One matter recorded as held, not as a defect: the addressee suffixes alternate inside the span -- וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ at oshb:Isa.51.12 against עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ at oshb:Isa.51.13 and בְּפִ֔יךָ at oshb:Isa.51.16 (byte tier). No morphology layer is staged and the second witness does not distinguish these forms, so the addressee question stays open; the row does not decide it, which is the correct handling.

items.claim: The close seam is argued from a non-initial imperative while the verse-initial divine messenger frame just past it is never engaged, a book-wide two-site cup pair crosses the cut undisclosed, and the paragraph layer is cited only on the side that corroborates.
items.evidence: Positional claim contradicted by the bytes: the row says twice that a fresh imperative 'opens' web:Isa.51.21, but that verse is verse-initial לָכֵ֛ן with שִׁמְעִי only in second position (oshb:Isa.51.21, byte tier). Verse-initial position is the operative test this book's frame spine uses -- the oracle headers are verse-initial at all ten of their sites and the woe-cry at 20 of its 22 verses -- so a non-initial imperative is not an opener in the sense the argument needs. The row concedes the connective in its rejected alternative and then argues as though it were absent. The strongest frame at this seam is left unengaged: oshb:Isa.51.22 opens verse-initially with כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֨יִךְ֙ (byte tier) -- a DIVINE messenger frame borne by a suffixed title with an intervening element, not a royal-messenger use. The row lists that verse and the one after it among its evidence but never names the frame or whose it is, although it is the only messenger-formula site in ch 51 (sweep: 48 verses book-wide, 8 in chs 49-52) and the one tier-1 signal in this neighbourhood. Undisclosed cross-seam device: the cup-of-staggering vocabulary binds this row's opening verse to a verse three past its close -- the run אֶת קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס is shared by oshb:Isa.51.17 and oshb:Isa.51.22 from accent-stripped tier down (byte tier separates them), and its distinctive noun stands at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier -- oshb:Isa.51.17 and oshb:Isa.51.22). That argues the movement runs to 51:23, which is the rival the row rejects. Disclosure asymmetry: the row cites the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.16 for its front seam and says nothing at its own close, where the inventory's next mark falls at oshb:Isa.51.21 (SAMEKH, single-witness) -- one verse PAST the cut, grouping 51:17-51:21 across it. The layer is weak corroboration in the Prophets, is never a driver, and its absence at 51:20 is not counterevidence; the defect is engaging the layer only where it helps. No ketiv/qere note stands in ch 51, so nothing is owed there. Confirmed sound: the onset הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י is verse-initial, matches the source bytes at byte tier and is genuinely doubled (two tokens, oshb:Isa.51.17); the stem contrast with the earlier awake-cry is correctly drawn and not harmonized; the unit-type deviation is disclosed.
